title: Commonworld Atlas list page
description: One page of 50 published entries (/api/v1/atlas/page/{page}.json, /api/v1/atlas/categories/{category}/page/{page}.json, /api/v1/atlas/platforms/page/{page}.json for the A-Z list). Start at page 1 and follow `next` until `has_more` is false. Every page of one build carries the same `snapshot_id`; if it changes between two pages, the list was rebuilt in between: start again from page 1. When a list gets shorter, a page number that existed before and is now past the last page answers HTTP 302 (temporary, never cached) to that list's last page, for example page 8 -> page 7 after the list shrank from 8 pages to 7; the page you land on has a different `page` than you asked for and a new `snapshot_id`, so start again from page 1. The redirect goes away when the list grows back and the page exists again (plain HTTP 200). A page number that never existed (0, not a number, or above the highest page ever built) returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body (application/json). Added in schema_version 1.8.0.

generated_at.description: Time of the newest data in this build, ISO 8601 UTC: the later of source_snapshot_at and newest_observation, so it moves when a card is amended (since schema_version 1.9.0; before, it was the source snapshot time alone).

source_snapshot_at.description: Time the source data snapshot file was produced, ISO 8601 UTC (what generated_at held before schema_version 1.9.0).

newest_observation.description: Newest observed_at of any published claim, ISO 8601 UTC; never later than generated_at.

snapshot_id.description: Id of the published list: the same on every page of one build; it changes when an entry is added, removed or changed, not with the daily link-safety check or a new screenshot.

has_more.description: true when a next page exists.

next.description: URL of the next page, or null on the last page.

prev.description: URL of the previous page, or null on page 1.

full_list.description: The complete list in one file (platforms.json or the category file).
